Share the structure direction, approximate dimensions, jewelry and insert layout, artwork and finish preferences, expected quantity for each design, destination country and target timing. Confirm currency, quantity basis, trade terms, destination and validity before comparing offers.

A counter display carton holds a group of retail items in a box or tray that is prepared for presentation on a counter. Consider this direction when a small brand needs the retailer to display several packaged gifts without arranging each one independently. Define the delivery state, setup steps and customer removal sequence so the display proposal covers both transport to the retailer and use on the counter.

A rigid paperboard postal envelope encloses a flat item through a defined opening and closing flap. Consider this direction for a small printed gift or another flat configuration when the proposed panel construction and opening process suit the contents. Record the complete packed thickness, corners and customer access so the envelope can be assessed as a finished parcel, rather than as an empty flat shape.

A hanging-tab carton adds a display panel or attachment above or beside a folding box so the pack can be presented on a retail fixture. Consider this direction when the product should remain inside a carton while the retailer hangs the pack. Brief the fixture interface, assembled weight and product position together, then review the complete package in the intended display arrangement.

Paired corrugated end caps are internal supports placed around specified ends of a product or an inner pack. Consider this direction when the proposed outer carton needs a defined relationship to those end areas. Record the product geometry, contact points and loading sequence so the two supports are designed and reviewed with the enclosure rather than chosen as separate pieces.

A regular slotted shipping carton uses a joined body with top and bottom flaps that are closed after forming and loading. Consider this outer-pack direction when a retail gift, several small boxes or a coordinated set needs a defined shipping unit. Start with the complete inner arrangement and closure process so the carton proposal covers what is actually packed and sent.

A shoulder and neck rigid box uses an inner board section around the base to guide the lid and define the visible opening. Consider this direction when a jewelry or candle gift needs a lift-off reveal with a deliberate display height. Brief the base, inner neck, lid and product holder together so an attractive closed box also opens comfortably around the actual contents.

An auto-lock bottom carton uses a prepared bottom arrangement that opens into position as the carton is formed. Consider this direction when a packing process needs to set up a retail carton before loading a candle vessel or small gift. The useful brief explains how the base opens, how the contents bear on it and what the packing team must verify before closing the top.

A jewelry mounting card uses holes, slots or another proposed attachment arrangement to present a piece on a printed card. Consider this direction when earrings, a necklace or a small set needs a defined display position inside a pouch, gift box or retail presentation. Plan the jewelry geometry, attachment and back of the card before choosing the front artwork.

Keep any partial-load arrangement deliberate. 'Half full' should describe which rows remain, not simply half the initial unit count placed wherever convenient. Photograph that starting pattern and ask whether staff must move units forwards. This gives the base and access review one repeatable configuration without turning a casual trial into a capacity claim.

Prepare custom molded pulp inserts around the product you need to pack, the box they will sit in and the way customers remove the contents. Share your dimensions, quantities and destination with Packrivo. We coordinate packaging sourcing questions with independent suppliers so the proposed construction, sample and quotation can address the same requirements.

A folded box liner is an internal component formed against the walls or selected surfaces of a box. Consider this direction when the brief needs to describe where the product or its retail pack meets the surrounding enclosure. Plan the liner's coverage, folds and loading sequence first, then decide whether a separate holder is needed to locate the contents.

Write the before-load base inspection as a visible condition from the confirmed drawing. Staff need to know where to look, not only that they should 'check the bottom'. Keep the inspection view available while the carton is empty. If the supplier changes a tab, revise the instruction photo and the observation field before using that new carton at the bench.

A corrugated book-wrap mailer folds around a flat item or stack to form its outer pack. Consider this direction for a printed gift, notebook or other flat product when the proposed wrapping panels, edge treatment and sealing can be reviewed together. Describe the packed thickness and corner geometry first so the wrap is evaluated around the real contents.

A gable-top carton forms a raised top with a carrying feature above the main box body. Consider this direction for a gift that will be handed over and carried, when the proposed handle, top closure and base can be reviewed with the full contents. Describe the carry action alongside the product layout so the handle becomes a defined part of the structure.

Describe whether the closed lid should cover the neck completely or leave part visible. Then identify the product's highest point, including clasps, lids, bows or a folded care card. Keep that height separate from the box's exterior height. A holder that raises the product can change lid clearance even when the outer dimensions stay the same.

A tab-lock roll-end corrugated pack needs its offered wall folds, locking tabs and receivers drawn together. Review those interfaces around the complete inner pack and the intended opening route. The catalogue establishes a named direction; the actual proposal establishes which lock and folding actions the packing team will use.

This direction concerns an outer carton with an interlocking base and slotted top flaps. Supplier terminology can vary. Request a drawing and photographed bottom-closing sequence that identify the carton as delivered, the tab order and the final engagement. Keep the supplied state explicit when a supplier uses the term '1-2-3'.
